newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blasts Croatia for giving medal to suspect.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blasts Croatia for giving medal to suspect.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday blasted Croatia for awarding a medal to a former Bosnian Croat army commander indicted for war crimes, calling the move "wholly inappropriate."

"The United States believes it is completely inappropriate to bestow a military decoration on a person who is under indictment by the (U.N. War Crimes) Tribunal ... and it does raise questions about their commitment to Dayton" peace accords, State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies told reporters.

He spoke after Slobodna Dalmacija newspaper reported that Gen. Tihomir Blaskic was decorated by Croatian President Franjo Tudjman for his part in Croatia's 1995 recapture of the rebel Serb enclave of Knin Krajina in southern Croatia.

Blaskic, who surrendered to The Hague-based tribunal in April, is charged with crimes against Moslem civilians in central Bosnia during Moslem-Croat war in 1992 and 1993 when he was commander of Bosnian Croat forces.
He was promoted to a senior post in Croatia's regular army after his indictment by the court.

Davies said awarding the medal "sends a signal of support for him (Blaskic) ... a signal that his wartime service is appreciated, when -- if the indictment is to be believed -- there is some question about how positive his wartime service was in any respect."
Davies said he did not know why Tudjman acted.

But another U.S. official told Reuters there is concern in the administration that Tudjman's severe stomach cancer -- which officials say has spread to his lymph nodes -- may have made him "a man with nothing to lose who is determined to do what he wants to."
Officials say they have been told Tudjman, who was treated last month at a government hospital in Washington, D.C., has only a few months to live.

Such a condition could spur a person "to be a force for good or ill...depending on how he perceives his legacy and whether he wants the approbation of the international community" or cares more about cementing his image at home, one official said.
Awarding the medal to Blaskic appears to suggest that Tudjman is more concerned about burnishing his credentials as a nationalist, the official said.
The war crimes court has indicted over 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for alleged war crimes but has only seven in custody. Blaskic's trial is due to begin in the spring.
